title.narrative: Mine Survey and Clearance Program in Omdurman, Sudan

description.narrative: ltpgtLed by the national NGO JASMAR, with the technical support and oversight of the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), two Multi Task Teams (MTT) and one Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Team will work to carry out Non-Technical Survey to define where Explosive Ordnance (EO) are to be found in Omdurman. With a priority focus on critical social infrastructure, such as health facilities, markets, and schools, these teams will define Suspected Hazardous Areas (SHA) and Confirmed Hazardous Areas (CHA) where further investigation and/or clearance needs to take place. Where appropriate, this will be followed by the safe removal of the explosive ordnance to areas designated by the National Mine Action Center (NMAC). The project will improve the security and safety of 11,500 beneficiaries and facilitate the scale up of the famine response in Omdurman through the creation of a safer operating environment for humanitarians. The integrated capacities, managed by JASMAR, and technically trained and supported by DRC, will work to address safety gaps in ongoing HMA activities conducted across community actors and local authorities, whilst providing initial technical investments in local HMA capacities that are critical to the ongoing emergency response in Omdurman. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThis project aims to leverage the current communally led survey and clearance work being conducted by volunteers and supported by NMAC in Omdurman. This work, born of necessity due to the nature of the conflict demonstrates the importance of this project. It requires training and accreditation to ensure that international safety standards are met and, where possible, volunteers are professionalized, trained and integrated into teams in a way that is appropriate to the high-risk nature of this work. Thus, JASMAR will assess the current volunteers and hire those who demonstrate the capacity to pass this accreditation process. This process will be carried out in coordination with NMAC to ensure that it is in line with their strategy for urban clearance operations. By engaging through existing community-based structures, the project aims to quickly build a comprehensive picture of contamination in this environment by leveraging the information of multiple networks. ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThus, once trained and accredited two MTT will execute surface-only Battle Area Clearance (BAC) principles, in line with NMAA definitions, as well as surveying infrastructure to determine if it is safe or unsafe through physical inspection. The teams will mark the areas either green (safe) or red (unsafe) and the community will then be informed as well as receive explosive ordnance risk education (EORE) outlining how best to protect themselves around areas registered as Confirmed Hazardous (CHA). The MTTs will inspect key social infrastructure such as hospitals, schools, shops and markets and inform the community of the status of each site. The Humanitarian Community and other agencies will be informed by means of a regular infrastructure status report. Once a CHA is registered all possible measures are to be implemented to avoid access by community and possible injuries. The EOD team with an EOD level 3 qualified TL, will visit the CHAs and inspect the reported EO. If this EO is found “Safe to Move” it will be collected and stored at a dedicated safe storage area identified by NMAC until demolitions are allowed. The team setup and planned coordination with NMAC / NMAA are designed based on gaps and restrictions in the local context, including prohibitions on demoiltions by humanitarian actors, safefy gaps identified in ongoing community / NMAC activities, as well as an urgent need to mitigate risks around infrastructure currently being accessed and used by civilian populations across Omdurman The current expectations are to find Unexploded Ordnance (UXO), ordnance which was fired and failed to function, as well as abandoned explosive ordnance (AXO), which was left behind by combatants and is no longer under their control. ltbrgtlt/pgt
